title: Harborview Pension Fund: Contoso Equity Fund Class C fees and committee review
description: Hero call. Two Harborview colleagues evaluate a large-cap core mandate. The analyst assumes Class A, the CIO corrects it to Class C (their platform only lists C). The seller commits to a fee comparison and an updated fact sheet with two different due-date phrasings; the CIO's committee hand-off is a customer commitment and must not become a seller task.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Good morning, Dana, and good morning, Alex. Thanks for making the time.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Morning, Sam. Happy to. It has been pouring since the weekend here, so I'm glad to be inside with a coffee.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Ha, I know that feeling. We had a gray, wet weekend on my end too, so I'm hoping it clears up soon. Shall we get started?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Please. We're pulling together our large-cap core mandate, and Alex has been doing most of the screening work.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Thanks, Dana. Hi, Sam. I had the Class A shares of the Contoso Equity Fund in my notes, so my main question is how the front-end sales charge would work on a position our size.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Hold on, Alex, it's not the Class A shares. We're looking at the Contoso Equity Fund, Class C, because that's the only one our custodian's platform lists.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Thanks for the catch, Dana. So that's Class C, which means no front-end load, but there's an ongoing distribution fee and a deferred sales charge if you redeem in the first year.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Got it. What's the total expense ratio on Class C, and how does it stack up against what we'd pay on Class A?

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Class C runs about one point six percent all in, and Class A is closer to ninety-five basis points before any sales charge. On a large position that gap matters, so the breakpoints are worth a look as well.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's helpful. Could you put the numbers in writing, class by class? Our investment committee will want to see them before they approve anything.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Absolutely. I'll send you the fee comparison by Friday, with the expense ratios and the sales charge schedule side by side.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Thanks. The other thing is that our file still has an old one-pager from last quarter, so I'm not sure the holdings and expense figures are current.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Good catch. Let me get the updated fact sheet over to you tomorrow.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Perfect. Once I have both, I'll take them to our investment committee when it meets, and I'll let you know how it goes.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: That sounds great. And if the committee ever wants a lower-cost share class down the road, a conversion is straightforward once you're past the breakpoints.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Good to know. Is there a due diligence questionnaire we should expect to fill out on our side?

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Not for a fund your platform already lists, but your committee may have its own checklist. Dana, you would know better than I would.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: We do have a short internal form, but my team handles that on our end, so there's nothing for you to complete.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Perfect, that keeps it simple. Anything else on your mind before we wrap up?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No, I think that covers it. Thanks, Sam.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Same here. Enjoy the rest of your week.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: You too, both of you. Stay dry out there.

gold.notes: Class A is mentioned by Alex and rejected by Dana, so only Class C (SYN-000002) is a gold product. Dana taking the material to the investment committee is a customer commitment, not a seller task. 'By Friday' resolves to 2026-11-13 and 'tomorrow' to 2026-11-11 for a Tuesday call.
